description: Phase 4 employee-level goldens for tax-classification paths the earlier phases do not exercise: de minimis ceilings and the shared PHP 90,000 other-benefits pool, leave monetization tax treatment, approved year-end tax adjustment settlement, and approved minimum-wage-earner classification. Every expected value is a literal computed by hand from the cited rules, never from PayrollPH functions.

sources.deMinimis: BIR RR No. 29-2025 (amending RR 2-98), effective January 6, 2026: rice subsidy ceiling PHP 2,500 per month; excess over a de minimis ceiling is an 'other benefit' counted toward the PHP 90,000 exclusion (NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7)(e) as amended by TRAIN).
sources.leaveMonetization: NIRC Sec. 32(B)(7) and RR 29-2025: monetized unused vacation leave of a private employee up to 12 days is de minimis; any amount flagged taxable is ordinary compensation.
sources.withholding: BIR RR No. 11-2018 Annex E semi-monthly table effective January 1, 2023: 0 up to 10,417; 15% over 10,417; 937.50 + 20% over 16,667; 4,270.70 + 25% over 33,333.
sources.mwe: NIRC Sec. 24(A)(2) as amended by TRAIN and RR 11-2018 Sec. 2.78.1(B)(13): the statutory minimum wage of a minimum wage earner, with holiday, overtime, night-shift differential and hazard pay, is exempt; other taxable compensation is taxed at graduated rates (Soriano v. Secretary of Finance, G.R. 184450, 2017). NCR Wage Order NCR-26: PHP 695 daily.
sources.sss: SSS Circular 2024-006 (January 2025): 15% total, 5% employee on the MSC; EC PHP 30 for MSC PHP 15,000 and above.
sources.philHealth: PhilHealth Advisory 2025-0002: 5% premium split equally, PHP 10,000 floor.
sources.pagIbig: HDMF Circular 460: 2% employee and employer on a PHP 10,000 maximum fund salary.

assumptions: First semi-monthly cutoff with 50/50 split statutory collection, no attendance, leave, loans or retro pay.

SSS compensation is all actual remuneration in the month (RA 11199 Sec. 8(f)), so de minimis and leave monetization raise the SSS MSC up to the PHP 35,000 cap; PhilHealth stays on monthly basic salary (Advisory 2025-0002) and Pag-IBIG is capped at the PHP 10,000 fund salary. The year-end settlement and the allowance flagged outside the SSS/Pag-IBIG base do not move contributions. PRACTITIONER REVIEW: confirm SSS treatment of de minimis and monetized leave.
The PHP 30,000 baseline matches Phase 2A EMP-006: gross 15,000.00, SSS 750.00, PhilHealth 375.00, Pag-IBIG 100.00, taxable 13,775.00, withholding 503.70.

The MWE pair is paid exactly the NCR minimum (PHP 16,680 monthly / 24 standard days = PHP 695.00 daily). Monthly 16,680: SSS MSC 16,500 (EE 412.50 per cutoff), PhilHealth EE 208.50, Pag-IBIG EE 100.00; EE total 721.00 per cutoff.

MWE taxable compensation follows BIR Form 2316: gross less the statutory minimum wage and less employee mandatory contributions (both are separate non-taxable items). PRACTITIONER REVIEW: confirm the contribution exclusion for an MWE with other taxable compensation.

deMinimisWithinCeiling.description: Rice subsidy PHP 2,000/month (PHP 1,000 this cutoff) is inside the PHP 2,500 monthly ceiling: fully exempt from tax. SSS remuneration becomes 32,000 (MSC 32,000, EE 800 per cutoff); taxable 16,000 - 1,000 - 800 - 375 - 100 = 13,725; withholding 15% x (13,725 - 10,417) = 496.20.

deMinimisExcessIntoPool.description: Rice subsidy PHP 6,000/month (PHP 3,000 this cutoff): PHP 2,500 exempt as de minimis, PHP 500 excess moves to the PHP 90,000 pool, which still has room, so nothing extra is taxed. SSS remuneration 36,000 caps at MSC 35,000 (EE 875); taxable 15,000 - 1,350 = 13,650; withholding 15% x 3,233 = 484.95.

deMinimisExcessAfterExhaustedPool.description: Same PHP 500 excess when a released June payroll already used the full PHP 90,000 pool: the excess is taxable. Taxable 13,650 + 500 = 14,150; withholding 15% x (14,150 - 10,417) = 559.95.

leaveConversionExempt.description: 5 vacation-leave days monetized at PHP 1,363.64 (PHP 6,818.20), within the 12-day de minimis limit and flagged exempt: not taxed. SSS remuneration caps at MSC 35,000 (EE 875); taxable 13,650; withholding 484.95.

leaveConversionTaxable.description: The same PHP 6,818.20 flagged taxable is ordinary compensation: taxable 13,650 + 6,818.20 = 20,468.20; withholding 937.50 + 20% x (20,468.20 - 16,667) = 1,697.74.

yearEndRefund.description: Approved 2026 year-end refund of PHP 1,200 settled on the December 1-15 cutoff: cutoff withholding and taxable unchanged, net rises by exactly the refund. The refund prints as a deduction credit (-1,200), so printed earnings (15,000.00) and deductions (528.70) reconcile to the stored buckets.

yearEndCollection.description: Approved 2026 year-end additional tax of PHP 800 collected on the December 1-15 cutoff: cutoff withholding unchanged, net falls by exactly the collection.

mweTaxableAllowance.description: Approved NCR minimum wage earner with a PHP 12,000 taxable allowance: the minimum wage (8,340) and contributions (721) are non-taxable, so taxable = 20,340 - 8,340 - 721 = 11,279; withholding 15% x (11,279 - 10,417) = 129.30.

nonMweTaxableAllowance.description: Identical worker and allowance without an MWE classification: taxable 8,340 - 721 + 12,000 = 19,619; withholding 937.50 + 20% x (19,619 - 16,667) = 1,527.90. Proves the MWE exemption is real, not a coincidence of low pay.

limitations: Engineering evidence only: not a substitute for independent CPA/payroll-practitioner sign-off, parallel payroll cycles or BIR acceptance.
The engine honors the stored leave-conversion tax flag; this catalog does not prove that more than 12 monetized days can never be flagged exempt.
Year-end adjustment amounts are taken as approved inputs; the annualization that produces them is not recomputed here.
Year-end refund: only net, withholding, taxable, contributions and gross are asserted, and the payslip is checked as printed total = net, because of the known bucket finding recorded on that case.
